newsitem.title: JAPAN: HANDBALL-CHAMPIONS FRANCE CRASH TO S.KOREA.
newsitem.headline: HANDBALL-CHAMPIONS FRANCE CRASH TO S.KOREA.

text.p: World champions France crashed to a 27-26 defeat against Asian powerhouse South Korea but Olympic silver medallists Sweden maintained their momentum at the men's handball world championship on Tuesday.

France seemed set to record their second win of the tournament when they took a 18-11 lead into the halftime break but a spirited fightback engineered by Yoon Kyung-shin and Cho Boem-yon carried the Koreans to victory.
Yoon, top scorer at the 1995 world championship in Iceland, spun home the winner towards the dying stages of the match.
Cho Boem-yon top scored for the Koreans with nine goals, while Yoon netted eight. Gueric Kervadec led the French with nine goals.
Sweden rallied to a 24-17 win against Norway to take control of group B with their second win.
Staffan Olsson top-scored for Sweden with six goals. Magnus Wislander and Stefan Loevgran both netted five.
Olympic bronze medallists Spain were held to a 19-19 draw by Egypt, while the Czech Republic notched their first win, 24-10 over Brazil in group C.
Sherif Hegazy scored five goals for Egypt and Enric Masip Barras netted five for Spain.
The Czech Republic were led by Tomas Bokr, who scored five goals.
The top four teams in each group will advance to the final rounds starting next week.
